# REGENT OF DHARMASRAYA

# NUMBER 16 OF 2018

# CONCERNING

# WOMEN EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

# BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY

# THE REGENT OF DHARMASRAYA,

Considering:  
a. that women and children have the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity; b. that women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence, therefore they need to receive optimal protection;  
c. that the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children as well as the improvement of the quality of life of women and children, is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on Women Empowerment and Child Protection;  

In View of:  
1. Article 18 paragraph (6) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia;  

2. Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2002 Number 109, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4236) as amended several times most recently by Law Number 17 of 2016 concerning the Stipulation of Government Regulation in Lieu of Law Number 1 of 2016 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection into Law (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2016 Number 237, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5946);  
3. Law Number 38 of 2003 concerning the Establishment of Dharmasraya Regency, South Solok Regency and West Pasaman Regency in West Sumatra Province (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2003 Number 153, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number
4348. ;  
4. Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2004 Number 95, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number
4419. ;  
5. Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2014), as amended several times, most recently by Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning the Third Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2014);  
6. Regional Regulation of West Sumatra Province Number 5 of 2013 concerning the Protection of Women and Children (Regional Gazette of West Sumatra Province of 2013 Number 5, Supplement to the Regional Gazette of West Sumatra Province Number 88);  

With the Mutual Approval of THE REGIONAL HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES OF DHARMASRAYA REGENCY and

To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING WOMEN EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

7. Pengarusutamaan Gender adalah strategi yang dilakukansecara rasional dan sistimatis untuk mencapai danmewujudkan kesetaraan dan keadilan gender dalamsejumlah aspek kehidupan manusia, melalui kebijakandanprogram yang memperhatikan pengalaman, aspirasi,kebutuhan dan permasalahan perempuan dan laki – laki kedalam perencanaan, pelaksanaan, pemantauandanevaluasi dari seluruh kebijakan dan programdiberbagai bidangkehidupan dan pembangunan.

## Bagian Kedua

Asas, Tujuan dan Ruang Lingkup

#### Pasal 2

1. Penyelenggaraan perlindungan perempuan berdasarkanasas:a. kepentingan terbaik bagi perempuan;  
b. keadilan gender dan kesetaraan gender; c. kearifan lokal; dand. kepastian hukum.  
2. Penyelenggaraan perlindungan anak berdasarkanasas: a. non diskriminasi;  
b. kepentingan yang terbaik bagi anak;  
c. hak untuk hidup, kelangsungan hidup, danperkembangan;  
d. penghargaan terhadap pendapat anak; dan e. kepastian hukum.

#### Pasal 3

Pemberdayaan perempuan dan Perlindungan anak bertujuan: a. sebagai pedoman bagi pemerintah daerahdalamperencanaan, kebijakan dan strategi perlindunganperempuan dan anak;  
b. melindungi perempuan dan anak dari tindakan, keputusandan kebijakan yang melanggar hak perempuan dananak; c. mencegah terjadinya pelanggaran hak perempuandananak;  
d. meningkatkan pemberdayaan terhadap perempuandananak;  
e. meningkatkan peran dan nilai kearifan lokal sertaperananadat dalam perlindungan perempuan dan anak; danf. meningkatkan peran lembaga pemerintahdannonpemerintah di daerah dalam upaya perlindunganperempuandan anak.

#### Pasal 4

Ruang lingkup pengaturan perlindungan perempuandananakmeliputi:
a. hak dan kewajiban;  
b. peningkatan kualitas hidup perempuan;  
c. perlindungan perempuan dan anak; d. peningkatan kualitas keluarga;  
e. sistem data gender dan anak;  
f. pemenuhan hak anak;  
g. kabupaten layak anak; danh. pembinaan dan pengawasan.

#### Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Dharmasraya Regency.  
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration of Dharmasraya Regency.  
3. Regent is the Regent of Dharmasraya.  
4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Dharmasraya Regency.  
5. Social Service, Women Empowerment, Child Protection, Population Control and Family Planning hereinafter referred to as the Service is the Regional Apparatus that handles affairs in the Field of Implementation of Women and Child Protection.  
6. Women Protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment).  
7. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy carried out rationally and systematically to achieve and realize gender equality and justice in a number of aspects of human life, through policies and programs that take into account the experiences, aspirations, needs and problems of women and men in the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of all policies and programs in various fields of life and development.  
8. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group hereinafter referred to as Gender Mainstreaming Pokja is a consultation forum for implementers and drivers of gender mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region.  
9. Gender Mainstreaming Focal Point is an apparatus in the Regional Apparatus who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.  
10. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including children still in the womb.  
11. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.  
12. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children.  
13. Children's Forum is a forum for child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking.  
14. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.  
15. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.  
16. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.  
17. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.  
18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community.  
19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.  
20. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.  
21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive.  
22. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.  
23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.  
24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence.  
25. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the soul through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.  
27. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 28. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.  
29. Customs are eternal and hereditary codes of conduct from one generation to another generation as heritage, so that they are strongly integrated with the behavior patterns of society.

## Part Two

Principles, Objectives and Scope

#### Article 2

1. The implementation of women protection is based on the principles of: a. the best interests of women;  
b. gender justice and gender equality; c. local wisdom; and d. legal certainty.  
2. The implementation of child protection is based on the principles of: a. non-discrimination;  
b. the best interests of the child;  
c. the right to life, survival, and development;  
d. respect for the views of the child; and e. legal certainty.

#### Article 3

Women empowerment and child protection aim to: a. serve as a guide for regional government in planning, policies and strategies for the protection of women and children;  
b. protect women and children from actions, decisions and policies that violate the rights of women and children; c. prevent violations of the rights of women and children;  
d. increase empowerment of women and children;  
e. increase the role and value of local wisdom and the role of customs in the protection of women and children; and f. increase the role of government and non-government institutions in the region in efforts to protect women and children.

#### Article 4

The scope of regulation of women and child protection includes:
a. rights and obligations;  
b. improvement of women's quality of life;  
c. protection of women and children; d. improvement of family quality;  
e. gender and child data system;  
f. fulfillment of children's rights;  
g. child-friendly regency; and h. guidance and supervision.

### Paragraph 1

Rights of Women

text:
#### Pasal 5

Setiap perempuan berhak:
a. memperoleh perlindungan dari tindakan diskriminasi; b. memperoleh perlindungan dari eksploitasi ekonomi daneksploitasi seksual;  
c. memperoleh perlindungan dari kekerasan fisik, psikologis,seksual, dan penelantaran;  
d. memperoleh pekerjaan yang layak sesuai kemampuannya; e. memperoleh cuti kerja dengan menerima upah/gaji sesuai peraturan perundang-undangan;  
f. memperoleh pendidikan dan pengajaran di semuajenis,jenjang dan jalur pendidikan;  
g. mendapatkan perlindungan khusus dalampelaksanaanpekerjaan atau profesinya terhadap hal-hal yangdapatmengancam keselamatan dan atau kesehatannya berkenaandengan fungsi reproduksi perempuan; danh. pemilikan dan pengelolaan harta bersamadalamperkawinan sesuai dengan peraturan perundang-undangan.

### Paragraf 2

Hak Anak

#### Pasal 6

Setiap anak berhak:
a. untuk hidup, tumbuh, berkembang dan berpartisipasi secara wajar sesuai harkat dan martabat kemanusiaan; b. memperoleh perlindungan dari tindakan diskriminasi; c. memperoleh perlindungan dari eksploitasi ekonomi daneksploitasi seksual;  
d. memperoleh perlindungan dari kekerasan fisik, psikologis,seksual, dan penelantaran;  
e. atas suatu nama sebagai identitas diri danstatuskewarganegaraan;  
f. memperoleh akta kelahiran secara bebas biaya ; g. untuk memeluk agama dan beribadah menurut ajaranagamanya dengan bimbingan orang tua/wali; h. untuk tidak dipaksa berganti agama oleh orang tuaasuh,orang tua angkat dan oleh siapapun;  
i. untuk diakui dan mengetahui orang tuanya, dibesarkandandiasuh oleh orang tuanya sendiri;  
j. memperoleh pelayanan kesehatan dan jaminansosial sesuai dengan kebutuhan fisik, mental, spiritual, dan sosial. k. memperoleh pendidikan dan pengajaran sesuai denganminat dan bakatnya;  
l. memperoleh perawatan, pendidikan, pelatihan,meningkatkan diri dan kemampuan berpartisipasi dalamkehidupan bermasyarakat dan bernegara bagi anakpenyandang disabilitas fisik, mental dan berkebutuhankhusus;  
m. menyampaikan dan didengar pendapatnya; dann. beristirahat dan memanfaatkan waktu luangdemi pengembangan diri.

## Bagian Kedua

Kewajiban Pemerintah Daerah

#### Pasal 7

Kewajiban Pemerintah Daerah dalamupaya perlindunganterhadap perempuan meliputi:
a. menetapkan dan melaksanakan kebijakan programdankegiatan perlindungan terhadap hak perempuan; b. melakukan kerjasama dengan masyarakat dan/atauOrganisasi Kemasyarakatan dalampenyelenggaraanperlindungan perempuan sesuai peraturan perundang-undangan;  
c. melakukan rehabilitasi dan pemberdayaanterhadapperempuan yang menjadi korban tindak kekerasan; d. memberikan perlindungan khusus kepada perempuankorban tindak kekerasan dan perdagangan orang ; dane. melakukan tindakan preventif dalamrangka mencegahterjadinya pelanggaran terhadap hak perempuan.

#### Pasal 8

Kewajiban Pemerintah Daerah dalamupaya perlindunganterhadap anak meliputi:
a. menjamin hak asasi setiap anak tanpa diskriminasi; b. memberikan dukungan sarana dan prasaranadalampenyelenggaraan perlindungan anak;  
c. menjamin hak anak untuk menyampaikanpendapatsesuai dengan usia dan tingkat kecerdasan anak; d. menetapkan dan melaksanakan kebijakansertaprogram/kegiatan perlindungan terhadap hak anak; e. melakukan kerjasama dengan masyarakat dan/atauOrganisasi Kemasyarakatan dalampenyelenggaraanperlindungan anak sesuai peraturan perundang-undangan; f. melakukan rehabilitasi terhadap anak yang menjadi korbantindak kekerasan;  
g. memberikan perlindungan khusus kepada anakdalamsituasi darurat, anak yang berhadapan denganhukum, anak korban tindak kekerasan dan perdaganganorang, anak dari kelompok minoritas dan terisolasi, anaktereksploitasi secara ekonomi dan/atau seksual, anakyang menjadi korban penyalahgunaan narkotika, alkohol, psikotropika dan anak dengan HIV/AIDS;  
h. menyelenggarakan pendidikan inklusif bagi anakyangberkebutuhan khusus; dani. melakukan tindakan preventif dalamrangka mencegahterjadinya pelanggaran terhadap hak anak.

## Bagian Ketiga

#### Article 5

Every woman has the right to:
a. obtain protection from discriminatory acts; b. obtain protection from economic exploitation and sexual exploitation;  
c. obtain protection from physical, psychological, sexual violence, and neglect;

### Paragraph 2

Rights of Children

#### Article 6

Every child has the right to:
a. live, grow, develop and participate reasonably in accordance with human dignity; b. obtain protection from discriminatory acts; c. obtain protection from economic exploitation and sexual exploitation;  
d. obtain protection from physical, psychological, sexual violence, and neglect;  
e. a name as personal identity and citizenship status;  
f. obtain a birth certificate free of charge; g. embrace religion and worship according to the teachings of their religion with the guidance of parents/guardians; h. not to be forced to change religion by foster parents, adoptive parents and by anyone;  
i. be recognized and know their parents, be raised and cared for by their own parents;  
j. obtain health services and social security in accordance with physical, mental, spiritual, and social needs. k. obtain education and teaching in accordance with their interests and talents;  
l. obtain care, education, training, self-improvement and the ability to participate in community and state life for children with physical, mental disabilities and special needs;  
m. express and have their opinions heard; andn. rest and utilize leisure time for self-development.

## Part Two

Obligations of Regional Government

#### Article 7

The obligations of the Regional Government in efforts to protect women include:
a. establish and implement policy programs and activities for the protection of women's rights; b. cooperate with the community and/or Community Organizations in the implementation of women's protection in accordance with laws and regulations;  
c. carry out rehabilitation and empowerment of women who are victims of violence; d. provide special protection to women victims of violence and human trafficking; ande. take preventive action in order to prevent violations of women's rights.

#### Article 8

The obligations of the Regional Government in efforts to protect children include:
a. guarantee the human rights of every child without discrimination; b. provide support for facilities and infrastructure in the implementation of child protection;  
c. guarantee the right of children to express opinions in accordance with the age and level of intelligence of the child; d. establish and implement policies and programs/activities for the protection of children's rights; e. cooperate with the community and/or Community Organizations in the implementation of child protection in accordance with laws and regulations; f. carry out rehabilitation of children who are victims of violence;  
g. provide special protection to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children victims of violence and human trafficking, children from minority and isolated groups, children exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic abuse and children with HIV/AIDS;  
h. organize inclusive education for children with special needs; andi. take preventive action in order to prevent violations of children's rights.

## Part Three

Obligations of the Community

#### Article 9

1. The obligations of the community in efforts to protect women and children:a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of women and children;  
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; andc. supervise the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of women and children.  
2. Ninik mamak, alim ulama and cadiak pandai as well as bundo kanduang are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and children.  
3. The obligations of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

## Part Four

Obligations of Family and/or Parents

### Paragraph 1

Obligations Regarding the Protection of Women

#### Article 10

The family in efforts to protect the rights of women is obliged to:
a. protect women from conflict and domestic violence that degrades the dignity of women; b. provide equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; andc. prevent violations of women's rights in the household.

### Paragraph 2

Obligations Regarding the Protection of Children

#### Article 11

1. Parents in efforts to protect the rights of children are obliged to:a. care for, maintain, educate, and protect children; b. develop children in accordance with their abilities, talents, and interests;  
c. provide formal and non-formal education; d. guide children to behave in accordance with religion, ethics and morals as well as customs; and e. prevent marriage at the age of children. (2) In the event that parents do not exist, or their whereabouts are unknown, or due to a reason, cannot carry out their obligations and responsibilities, then the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1) may be transferred to the family.

2. Kartu identitas anak diterbitkan oleh Perangkat Daerahyangmembidangi kependudukan dan pencatatan sipil.

## Bagian Ketiga

Pemenuhan Hak Anak di bidang pendidikan

#### Pasal 55

Pemerintah Daerah menjamin terselenggaranya programwajibbelajar bagi Anak sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturanperundang-undangan.

#### Pasal 56

1. Setiap penyelenggara satuan pendidikan wajib memberikankesempatan kepada Anak untuk memperolehlayananpendidikan tanpa diskriminasi.  
2. Setiap penyelenggara satuan pendidikandilarangmengeluarkan Anak dari lembaga pendidikan kecuali adajaminan terhadap keberlangsungan pendidikan Anak.  
3. Dalam hal Anak korban tindak Kekerasan mengalami putussekolah, maka anak korban kekerasan diberikanpendidikanformal maupun non formal, dalam hal ini dilakukanolehpenyelenggara satuan pendidikan dan berkoordinasi denganUnit Pemberdayaan Perempuan dan Anak

#### Pasal 57

1. Setiap Anak berhak memperoleh pendidikan danpengajarandalam rangka pengembangan pribadinya dantingkatkecerdasannya sesuai dengan minat dan bakat.  
2. Setiap Anak berhak mendapatkan Perlindungandi satuanpendidikan dari kejahatan seksual dan Kekerasanyangdilakukan oleh pendidik, tenaga kependidikan, sesamapeserta didik, dan/atau pihak lain.

#### Pasal 58

1. Anak penyandang disabilitas dan Anak berkebutuhankhususdiberikan kesempatan yang sama untuk memperolehlayananpendidikan formal, nonformal dan informal, termasukprogram pendidikan inklusif.  
2. Pemerintah daerah menyediakan tenaga pendidikbagi pendidikan inklusif pada setiap satuan pendidikan.

## Bagian Keempat

Pemenuhan Hak Anak di bidang Kesehatan danSosial

#### Pasal 59

1. Pemerintah Daerah wajib menyelenggarakanlayanankesehatan yang komprehensif bagi Anak, agar setiapAnakmemperoleh derajat kesehatan yang optimal sejakdalamkandungan.  
2. Layanan kesehatan yang komprehensif sebagaimanadimaksud pada ayat (1) meliputi:a. upaya promotif, preventif, kuratif dan rehabilitatif untukpelayanan kesehatan dasar;  
b. pembebasan dari beban biaya bagi anak gizi buruk, anakpenyandang disabilitas, anak berkebutuhan khusus, anakyang terinfeksi HIV/ AIDS, pekerja anak, anakkorbanpenyalahgunaan narkotika, alkohol, psikotropikadanzat adiktif lainnya, anak yang menjadi korbankekerasan,dan anak korban perdagangan orang;  
3. Pemerintah Daerah, masyarakat, keluarga danorangtuawajib mengusahakan agar Anak yang lahir terhindar dari penyakit yang mengancam kelangsungan hidupdan/ataumenimbulkan kecacatan.

#### Pasal 60

1. Upaya promotif pelayanan kesehatan dasar sebagaimanadimaksud dalam Pasal 59 ayat (2) huruf a ditujukanuntukmeningkatkan derajat kesehatan secara lebih optimal.  
2. Upaya promotif sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dilakukan dengan memberikan sosialisasi ataupenyuluhankepada masyarakat mengenai pola hidup sehat yangmeliputi:a. pentingnya air susu ibu ekslusif bagi bayi;  
b. pentingnya imunisasi bagi balita;  
c. pola hidup bersih;  
d. pentingnya makanan bergizi; dan e. bahaya narkoba dan merokok.  
3. Selain upaya promotif sebagaimana dimaksud padaayat (2),Pemerintah Daerah dapat melakukan kegiatanlaindalamrangka penyeleggaraan kesehatan.

#### Pasal 61

1. Upaya preventif pelayanan kesehatan dasar sebagaimanadimaksud dalam Pasal 59 ayat (2) huruf a ditujukanuntukmencegah terjadinya penyakit atau permasalahankesehatan.  
2. Upaya sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dilakukandengan:a. mewajibkan pada ibu untuk pemberian ASI ekslusif padabayi sampai usia 6 (enam) bulan;  
b. pemberian imunisasi dan vitamin gratis pada bayi danbalita;  
c. pemberian makanan bergizi kepada balita dari keluargakurang mampu;  
d. mengoptimalkan peran posyandu untuk pelayanankesehatan bagi ibu dan balita;  
e. melakukan pemeriksaan kesehatan secara berkala; f. menyediakan sarana sanitasi dan air bersihdisetiapsekolah; dang. menyediakan fasilitas khusus menyusui atauruanganpojok ASI di instansi pemerintah atau dunia usaha.

#### Pasal 62

1. Upaya kuratif pelayanan kesehatan dasar sebagaimanadimaksud dalam Pasal 59 ayat (2) huruf a ditujukanuntukmencegah penyakit menjadi lebih parah melalui pengobatan.  
2. Pengobatan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dilaksanakan secara bebas biaya bagi anak yang berasal dari keluarga kurang mampu.

#### Pasal 63

1. Upaya rehabilitatif pelayanan kesehatan dasar sebagaimanadimaksud dalam Pasal 59 ayat (2) huruf a ditujukanuntukmemelihara dan memulihkan kondisi setelah sakit.  
2. Upaya rehabilitatif sebagaimana dimaksud padaayat (1) dilakukan melalui pemeriksaan kesehatan secara berkala.

#### Pasal 64

Pemerintah Daerah wajib menyelenggarakan KesejahteraanSosial bagi:
a. anak yang berhadapan dengan hukum; b. anak korban kekerasan yang tereksploitasi secara ekonomi; c. anak yang tidak mempunyai orang tua dan diasuholehpihak atau keluarga yang tidak mampu;  
d. anak korban bencana alam atau bencana sosial; dane. anak penyandang disabilitas.

## Bagian Kelima

Pemenuhan Hak Anak di bidang Ketenagakerjaan

#### Pasal 65

Pemerintah Daerah melakukan pengawasan berkala padasetiaporang/badan yang mempekerjakan Anak dalamupayaPerlindungan terhadap pekerja Anak.

#### Pasal 66

1. Setiap orang/badan dilarang mempekerjakan danmelibatkanAnak pada pekerjaan yang terburuk.  
2. Pekerjaan yang terburuk yang dimaksud dalamayat (1) meliputi:a. segala pekerjaan dalam bentuk perbudakanatausejenisnya;  
b. segala pekerjaan yang memanfaatkan, menyediakan, ataumenawarkan Anak untuk pelacuran, produksi pornografi,pertunjukan porno, atau perjudian;  
c. segala pekerjaan yang memanfaatkan, menyediakan, ataumelibatkan Anak untuk produksi dan perdaganganminuman keras, narkotika, psikotropika, danzat adiktiflainnya; dan/ataud. semua pekerjaan yang membahayakan kesehatan,keselamatan, atau moral Anak.

#### Article 52

1. The Regional Government in its efforts to fulfill the rights of Children is responsible for: a. establishing and implementing policies and programs/activities for the fulfillment of Children's rights;  
b. respecting and guaranteeing the human rights of every Child without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status of the Child, birth order of the Child, and physical and/or mental condition;  
c. strengthening and developing service provider institutions for improving family quality in realizing Children's rights;  
d. guaranteeing the Protection, care, and welfare of Children with due regard to the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, or other persons who are legally responsible for the Child;  
e. providing facilities and infrastructure in the implementation of the fulfillment of Children's rights;  
f. guaranteeing the right of Children to express opinions in accordance with the age and level of intelligence of the Child; g. conducting supervision and guidance in the context of implementing the fulfillment of Children's rights; and h. cooperating with the private sector and/or NGOs in the implementation of Child Protection; (2) The responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by Regional Apparatus in accordance with their duties and functions.

## Part Two

Fulfillment of Children's Rights in the field of Birth Registration and Child Identity

#### Article 53

1. The Regional Government is obliged to administer the birth registration of Children with the issuance of birth certificates. (2) Birth certificates as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be administered free of charge.

#### Article 54

1. To encourage increased data collection, protection and public services and to realize the best interests of children, every child under the age of 17 years must have a child identity card.  
2. Child identity cards shall be issued by the Regional Apparatus responsible for population and civil registration.

## Part Three

Fulfillment of Children's Rights in the field of education

#### Article 55

The Regional Government guarantees the implementation of compulsory education programs for Children in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

#### Article 56

1. Every organizer of an education unit must provide opportunities for Children to obtain educational services without discrimination.  
2. Every organizer of an education unit is prohibited from expelling Children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the Child's education.  
3. In the event that a Child victim of Violence experiences dropping out of school, then the child victim of violence shall be provided with formal or non-formal education, in this case carried out by the organizer of the education unit and in coordination with the Women and Child Empowerment Unit

#### Article 57

1. Every Child has the right to obtain education and teaching in the context of developing their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.  
2. Every Child has the right to receive Protection in education units from sexual crimes and Violence committed by educators, education personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.

#### Article 58

1. Children with disabilities and Children with special needs shall be given equal opportunities to obtain formal, non-formal and informal education services, including inclusive education programs.  
2. The regional government shall provide educators for inclusive education in every education unit.

## Part Four

Fulfillment of Children's Rights in the field of Health and Social Welfare

#### Article 59

1. The Regional Government is obliged to provide comprehensive health services for Children, so that every Child obtains an optimal degree of health from the womb.  
2. Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include: a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services;  
b. exemption from cost burdens for malnourished children, children with disabilities, children with special needs, children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse, children who are victims of violence, and child victims of trafficking in persons;  
3. The Regional Government, community, family and parents are obliged to ensure that Children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten the continuity of life and/or cause disability.

#### Article 60

1. Promotive efforts for basic health services as referred to in Article 59 paragraph (2) letter a are aimed at improving the degree of health in a more optimal manner.  
2. Promotive efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by providing socialization or counseling to the community regarding healthy lifestyles which include: a. the importance of exclusive breast milk for infants;  
b. the importance of immunization for toddlers;  
c. clean living patterns;  
d. the importance of nutritious food; and e. the dangers of drugs and smoking.  
3. In addition to promotive efforts as referred to in paragraph (2), the Regional Government may carry out other activities in the context of health administration.

#### Article 61

1. Preventive efforts for basic health services as referred to in Article 59 paragraph (2) letter a are aimed at preventing the occurrence of disease or health problems.  
2. Efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by: a. requiring mothers to provide exclusive breastfeeding to infants up to the age of 6 (six) months;  
b. providing free immunization and vitamins to infants and toddlers;  
c. providing nutritious food to toddlers from underprivileged families;  
d. optimizing the role of posyandu for health services for mothers and toddlers;  
e. conducting periodic health examinations; f. providing sanitation facilities and clean water in every school; and g. providing special breastfeeding facilities or breastfeeding corner rooms in government agencies or the business sector.

#### Article 62

1. Curative efforts for basic health services as referred to in Article 59 paragraph (2) letter a are aimed at preventing diseases from becoming more severe through treatment.  
2. Treatment as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out free of charge for children from underprivileged families.

#### Article 63

1. Rehabilitative efforts for basic health services as referred to in Article 59 paragraph (2) letter a are aimed at maintaining and restoring conditions after illness.  
2. Rehabilitative efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through periodic health examinations.

#### Article 64

The Regional Government is obliged to administer Social Welfare for:
a. children in conflict with the law; b. child victims of violence who are economically exploited; c. children who do not have parents and are cared for by parties or families who are unable;  
d. child victims of natural disasters or social disasters; and e. children with disabilities.

## Part Five

Fulfillment of Children's Rights in the field of Employment

#### Article 65

The Regional Government conducts periodic supervision of every person/entity that employs Children in efforts to Protect child workers.

#### Article 66

1. Every person/entity is prohibited from employing and involving Children in the worst forms of work.  
2. The worst forms of work referred to in paragraph (1) include: a. all work in the form of slavery or the like;  
b. all work that utilizes, provides, or offers Children for prostitution, pornography production, pornographic performances, or gambling;  
c. all work that utilizes, provides, or involves Children for the production and trade of alcoholic beverages, narcotics, psychotropics, and other addictive substances; and/or d. all work that endangers the health, safety, or morals of Children.

# CHAPTER VIII

## CHILD-FRIENDLY REGENCY

#### Article 68

1. In the context of fulfilling Children's rights in an integrated, systematic and sustainable manner, the Regional Government establishes a policy for the Development of CFC.  
2. The policy for the Development of CFC as referred to in paragraph (1) contains:a. the concept of CFC concerning objectives, strategies and roles of related parties;  
b. children's rights; andc. the approach to CFC development.

#### Article 69

1. The policy for CFC development is directed at fulfilling Children's rights which are divided into 5 (five) groups, comprising: a. civil rights and freedoms;  
b. family environment and alternative care; c. basic health and welfare;  
d. education, leisure time utilization, and cultural activities; ande. special protection.  
2. Further provisions regarding the policy for CFC development as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent's Regulation.

#### Article 70

1. In order to ensure the effectiveness of CFC policy implementation in the Region, a CFC Task Force is established.  
2. The CFC Task Force as referred to in paragraph (1) has the principal duties of:a. coordinating the implementation of CFC policies and development;  
b. conducting socialization, advocacy and communication of information and education on CFC policies;  
c. collecting basic data for CFC development; d. conducting needs analysis sourced from basic data;  
e. disseminating basic data;  
f. determining the focus and priority of programs in realizing CFC, which are adjusted to regional potential;  
g. preparing a five-year Child-Friendly City regional action plan and work mechanism; and h. conducting monitoring, evaluation and reporting at least once (one time) a year.  
3. The establishment of the CFC Task Force as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by Regent's Decree.

#### Article 71

In carrying out its duties, the CFC Task Force as referred to in Article 70 paragraph (1) may coordinate and cooperate with the UPTD PPA and/or other institutions that provide Protection and Child services.

# CHAPTER IX

## GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

#### Article 72

1. The Regional Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.  
2. The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) comprises: a. the formulation of policies and regulations that serve as guidelines and standards in organizing women's empowerment and child protection; b. technical guidance and training, comprising:
1. providing training for government officials and law enforcement officers on the prevention and handling of violence;  
2. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;  
3. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;  
4. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; and
5. providing training to GMS working groups and focal points of each Regional Apparatus for the preparation of activity programs based on gender-responsive planning and budgeting.  c. provision of facilities and infrastructure in organizing women's empowerment and child protection.  d. facilitation of the establishment of nagari that care for women and children; e. provision of information through print and electronic media related to the protection of women and children. (3) The supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) comprises: a. monitoring carried out in the form of submission of reports on the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs by the Head of Regional Apparatus to the Regent periodically once (one time) every 3 (three) months; and b. evaluation of the organization of women's empowerment and child protection periodically once (one time) every 3 (three) months carried out by the relevant Regional Apparatus (4) The results of supervision as referred to in paragraph (3) constitute evaluation material for the policy of women's empowerment and child protection programs.  
5. Further provisions regarding Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent's Regulation.

##### I. UMUM

Anak adalah amanah sekaligus karunia Tuhan Yang MahaEsa, yang senantiasa harus kita jaga karena dalam dirinya melekat harkat, martabat, dan hak-hak sebagai manusia yang harus dijunjungtinggi. Dari sisi kehidupan berbangsadanbernegara, anak adalah masa depan bangsa dan generasi peneruscita-cita bangsa, sehingga setiap anak berhak atas kelangsunganhidup, tumbuh, dan berkembang, berpartisipasi serta berhak atas perlindungandari tindak kekerasan dan diskriminasi serta hak sipil dan kebebasan.

##### CONCERNING

##### WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

##### I. GENERAL

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, women are expected to give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, noble in character, potential and of quality. Through the role of women in the family, society and the state, resilient generations will be born who will continue the ideals of the nation. As citizens of Indonesia, women also have the right to improve quality and develop themselves according to their abilities, dignity and honor.

Women and children need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of women's nature itself, women and children often become objects of venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so on. As assets and hope of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of violence that will hinder their growth and development.

To realize women's empowerment and child protection, support from laws and regulations is needed that can guarantee its implementation.

Although the protection of women's and children's rights has been regulated in national level laws and regulations, the fulfillment of women's and children's constitutional rights and the improvement of the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, so in providing protection to women and children, the Regional Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection regulates the following scope: a. rights of women and children;
b. obligations;
c. improvement of women's quality of life;
d. protection of women and children;
e. improvement of family quality;
f. gender and child data system;
g. fulfillment of children's rights;
h. child-friendly regency; and i. guidance and supervision.
